title: Extending an assignment at a splitting step
statement: Let $h$ and $b$ be Boolean literals, let $R$ be a finite list of Boolean literals, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $a$ be a truth assignment. Suppose every variable index occurring in $h$, $b$, or $R$ is less than $n$, and the clause formed by $h$, $b$, and $R$ is satisfied by $a$. Then there is an assignment $a'$ agreeing with $a$ on every index below $n$ that satisfies both the link clause consisting of $h$, $b$, and the positive literal for variable $n$, and the continuation clause consisting of the negative literal for variable $n$ followed by $R$.
hypotheses_covered: all variable indices in $h,b,R$ are below $n$
replaced:
Let a clause with head literal, a second literal $b$, and a tail have all its
variable indices below $n$, and let $a$ be an assignment satisfying it. Then there
is an assignment $a'$ agreeing with $a$ below $n$ such that $a'$ satisfies both the
link clause $[\mathrm{head},\, b,\, (n,\mathrm{true})]$ and the continuation clause
headed by $(n,\mathrm{false})$ followed by the tail; the fresh value $a'(n)$ is the
truth of the tail under $a$.
